title: COS 101 ( UNIZIK )  : BASIC COMPONENTS OF A COMPUTER
subject: COS 101

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a computer?
options: A tool used for sending messages
A machine that performs only math
A unit that stores files permanently
questions.explanation: A computer accepts data, processes it, and produces meaningful information.

questions.question: How many basic functions does a digital computer carry out?
questions.explanation: A digital computer carries out five functions: input, store, process, output, and control.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five functions of a computer?
questions.explanation: Printing is an output function, not one of the five core functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a core component of a computer?
questions.explanation: Core components include CPU, motherboard, power supply, RAM, and ROM.

questions.question: Which of the following is a peripheral device?
questions.explanation: Peripherals include keyboard, mouse, monitor, printer, scanner, and USB drive.

questions.question: Computer hardware refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Hardware is the collection of physical elements that constitutes a computer system.

questions.question: Which part of the CPU executes arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explanation: The ALU executes all arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Which CPU part controls and coordinates computer components?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit controls and coordinates computer components.

questions.question: Which CPU component stores data to be executed next?
questions.explanation: Registers store the data that is to be executed next.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main part of the CPU?
questions.explanation: The CPU comprises ALU, CU, and registers; hard disk is secondary storage.

questions.question: How many main parts does the CPU comprise?
questions.explanation: The CPU comprises three main parts: ALU, CU, and registers.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the Control Unit's role?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit controls and coordinates computer components.

questions.question: Which type of memory is volatile?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; data is erased when power is turned off.

questions.question: Which memory is permanent and cannot be modified?
questions.explanation: ROM is a permanent form of storage that does not allow data to be modified.

questions.question: Random Access Memory allows access to any memory cell if which is known?
questions.explanation: RAM is random access because any memory cell can be accessed directly if the row and column are known.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about ROM?
questions.explanation: ROM stays active regardless of whether power supply is turned on or off.

questions.question: Which of the following is a magnetic secondary storage device?
questions.explanation: A hard disk stores data on an electromagnetically charged surface.

questions.question: Which optical media has the largest storage capacity?
questions.explanation: Blu-ray discs can store up to 50 GB of data.

questions.question: The storage capacity of a standard CD is which of the following?
questions.explanation: CDs can store up to 700 megabytes of data.

questions.question: Which storage device uses flash memory chips?
questions.explanation: A flash disk is a storage module made of flash memory chips.

questions.question: Which of the following describes a flash disk's structure?
questions.explanation: Flash disks have no mechanical platters; the disk storage structure is emulated.

questions.question: How does RAM storage capacity compare to hard disk capacity?
questions.explanation: RAM typically holds 500 MB to 6 GB, while hard disks hold 80 GB to 1000 GB.

questions.question: Which of the following happens to RAM contents when the computer is turned off?
questions.explanation: RAM contents disappear when power is turned off or the computer crashes.

questions.question: Which statement about hard disk contents is correct?
questions.explanation: Hard disk contents remain when the power is turned off and when the computer crashes.

questions.question: RAM consists of which of the following?
questions.explanation: RAM consists of chips, while hard disks consist of platters.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the primary function of the motherboard?
questions.explanation: The motherboard acts as the central electrical circuit by connecting different parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the motherboard?
questions.explanation: The motherboard comprises the CPU, memory, and secondary storage devices.

questions.question: Motherboards are sensitive to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Motherboards may malfunction if exposed to high temperatures, pressure, or humidity.

questions.question: The power supply unit converts which of the following?
questions.explanation: The power supply unit converts high voltage electrical current to a low voltage.

questions.question: Which device ensures stable power supply during fluctuations?
questions.explanation: A UPS or uninterrupted power supply unit ensures that fluctuations do not impact performance.

questions.question: Laptops typically operate on which power source?
questions.explanation: Laptops operate on removable batteries that require periodic charging.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the primary function of a computer keyboard?
questions.explanation: The keyboard is used to input text, characters, and other commands.

questions.question: Which type of keyboard may be virtual?
questions.explanation: In many tablets and virtual PCs, the keyboard may also be virtual.

questions.question: Which feature helps keyboard use in low light?
questions.explanation: Many keyboards have a backlight to illuminate the keys for use at night or in low light.

questions.question: Which of the following determines a monitor's sharpness and quality?
questions.explanation: The resolution and pixel density of a monitor determines its sharpness and quality.

questions.question: Which of the following can reduce eye strain from monitor light?
questions.explanation: An anti-glare film or wearing glasses can minimise the effect of monitor light.

questions.question: Which monitor size is commonly used by graphics professionals?
questions.explanation: 21-inch monitors are mostly used by graphics professionals.

questions.question: Which of the following does a computer mouse control?
questions.explanation: The mouse controls the cursor and gives input to the system.

questions.question: Which mouse feature helps navigate long pages?
questions.explanation: A scrolling wheel helps users navigate a long page.

questions.question: Which printer type uses toner?
questions.explanation: Laser printers combine a magnetic roller with powdered ink called toner.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common maintenance task for printers?
questions.explanation: Printer maintenance includes regularly replacing ink cartridges and toner.

questions.question: Which of the following does higher RAM in a computer increase?
questions.explanation: The higher the RAM, the more its processing power and ability to run applications simultaneously.

questions.question: A USB flash drive uses which type of memory?
questions.explanation: A USB Flash Drive consists of a flash memory data storage device integrated with a USB interface.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: An input device sends data to a computer, and the mouse is a common example.

questions.question: What do input devices translate data into?
questions.explanation: Input devices translate data from a form humans understand to one the computer can work with.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pointing input device?
questions.explanation: A trackball is a pointing device like a mouse.

questions.question: Which input device captures images for a computer?
questions.explanation: A digital camera is an input device that captures images.

questions.question: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: An output device communicates results of data processing, and a monitor is a common example.

questions.question: What do output devices convert electronic information into?
questions.explanation: Output devices convert electronically generated information into human readable form.

questions.question: Which output device produces physical copies on paper?
questions.explanation: A printer generates a copy of virtual text or images on paper using ink.
